bullets.text: Full-year CR improved to 93.5 with pretax underwriting income of $1.1B; net income per share reached $1.93 (+30%) and comprehensive EPS was $2.06 (+16%); ROE approximated 18% and 19%.

Written premiums grew close to 6% to top $17B, continuing multi-year expansion above $15B in 2011 and $16B in 2012; premium growth reflected higher average rates early before customer growth accelerated.

Net auto customers increased 276,000, with most gains occurring in the last four months. Agency and Direct channels reported double-digit new application growth by mid-third quarter alongside reduced retention losses.

Flo's apron was highlighted to portray Progressive as working to make things better. The Superstore campaign starring Flo achieved some of its best response levels, and Policy Box delivered targeted messages.

Declared ~$0.49/share annual variable dividend and $1.00/share special dividend; fixed-income portfolio returned 1.7% with 2.6% pretax book yield; indexed equity portfolio returned 32.8% on a ~14% allocation.

Overall 2013 rate changes were minimal following significant 2012 increases. The 2012 rate earn-in pressured conversion and retention. State product managers made numerous adjustments seeking profitable growth across states.

Snapshot contributed over $2B in auto written premium, with high acceptance rates among mobile buyers. Progressive Home Advantage served over 1M customers through 11 unaffiliated underwriting partners.

Mobile transactions reached double-digit percentages across quoting, sales, and payments. Quoting and buying enhancements met 99% of consumer car-driver needs, and Keynote ranked Progressive.com the No. 1 insurance website for nine consecutive years.
Agency and Direct auto channels both achieved double-digit new application growth late in 2013; agency PHA distribution expanded to 23 states and DC through American Strategic Insurance partnership.

Honored longtime Chairman Peter B. Lewis following his passing late in 2013; reaffirmed core cultural values, target 96 combined ratio constant, and policy life expectancy priorities outlined in Exhibit A.
